URL: https://www.iranintl.com/en/202610015558
Iran International (English) — published 2026-10-01T02:56:55Z

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio ordered Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and his delegation to leave New York after US-Iran negotiations stalled, Axios reported Wednesday, an account Iran's UN mission rejected.
QUOTE (Iran's UN mission, post on X): "The Iranian delegation left New York on Monday evening, in accordance with the schedule that had also been communicated to the US Department of State in advance on September 17."
Axios cited a US official as saying Rubio "kicked out" the Iranian delegation after it had "overstayed their welcome." The US mission to the UN informed Iran's mission Monday evening that the delegation had to leave immediately, according to the report. Araghchi and his delegation headed to the airport several hours later and flew to Doha early Tuesday, Axios reported. A second source told Axios Araghchi had already been scheduled to leave Monday night.
AP separately reported, citing two US officials, that Rubio ordered Araghchi and his delegation to leave New York earlier than planned. According to AP, some accounts indicated Araghchi had planned to remain until Wednesday.
President Masoud Pezeshkian reiterated on Wednesday that his government was seeking to bring the Islamabad understanding to fruition. He did not comment directly on Trump's rejection of Iran's proposal.
Iranian press reaction (summarised by Iran International):
- Reformist daily Shargh: Araghchi's remarks carried the message that Tehran did not want its return to diplomacy read in Washington as a retreat from its nuclear positions. "The main issue in the coming days will not be whether Iran and the United States are talking to each other, but whether they can move from exchanging messages to an implement[able] formula."
- Reformist daily Etemad: warned the Strait of Hormuz could lose value as an Iranian bargaining tool the longer the confrontation continues.
- Kayhan editor-in-chief Hossein Shariatmadari: portrayed US demands for verifiable nuclear concessions as evidence Washington never intended to negotiate in good faith; called for non-attributable maritime interdictions, deployment of coastal anti-ship batteries and expanded targeting of Western-escorted vessels, arguing global energy markets must face an "unbearable cost" before Washington lifts its blockade.
- QUOTE (political analyst Mehdi Kharatian): "Do not be deceived by those who these days are flooding you with false and biased reports about the ineffectiveness of oil and the Strait."
- Commentator Ahmad Zeidabadi argued Washington's decision to send detailed feedback through Qatar showed a diplomatic off-ramp remained open, and proposed a two-stage approach including temporary IAEA monitoring protocols in return for phased easing of transit restrictions.
